title: FinCrime Policy Set
description: A versioned, jurisdiction-scoped set of deterministic rules. The set is what a firm hands to the engine, and what a `provenance.policy_set` reference names. It carries two kinds of policy: enforceable rules, evaluated by code, and procedural policies, which the agent follows and the evaluation suite measures. The distinction matters: a control a firm must be able to defend to a regulator is enforced by code, and a control that cannot be evaluated by code does not belong in the enforceable list. See ADR-0003.

jurisdictions.description: A rule set with no jurisdiction applies structurally everywhere. A 'global' scope is invalid: regulatory content is never jurisdiction-agnostic.

procedural_policies.description: Policies the agent follows as part of its procedure and the evaluation suite measures. They are named in a skill's manifest, and are not evaluated by the policy engine.

checksum.description: The sha256 of the canonical JSON of this document with the checksum field removed. Optional in a set being authored; `fincrime policy export` stamps it, and a set that carries a wrong checksum is rejected on load.

check.description: What the skill must do, stated so that a reviewer can tell whether it did.

measured_by.description: How compliance with this policy is measured. A procedural policy is measured by the evaluation suite, not by the policy engine.
